newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC HK bond index rose 0.37 pct to 121.83 in Dec.
newsitem.headline: HSBC HK bond index rose 0.37 pct to 121.83 in Dec.

text.p: HSBC Markets said on Friday its Hong Kong bond index rose to 121.83 in December, a 0.37 percent increase over November.
The sub-index for Hong Kong government paper increased by 0.32 percent, while the sub-index for non-Hong Kong government paper rose by 0.40 percent.

Compared with levels at end-December 1995, the overall index increased by 6.9 percent, the sub-index for Hong Kong government paper rose by 6.6 percent and the sub-index for non-Hong Kong government paper increased by 7.1 percent.
In December, the Hong Kong bond market focused attention on the implementation of the new Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system, HSBC Markets said.

It said the demand from banks for short-term bills as an intra-day liquidity tool kept the spread between interbank rates and bill yields at around 100 basis points, especially during the early stages of the RTGS implementation.

The Hong Kong dollar yield curve also steepened further, with yield differentials between two and 10 years widening from 168 to 185 basis points. The 10-year government benchmark yield finished firmer at 7.26 percent.
